text: The abstract-scan proposal overstates direct support. P says agents have model-size-linked energy costs, job allocation changes under cooperative incentives, and recommendations support coordination, but it does not say agents privately observe and report a capability type. Q says peer scoring and coupled rewards are applications and that capabilities may be concealed but not counterfeited, but its supplied abstract gives neither payoff formulas nor the conditions for those variants. Thus a faithful implementation and a truthful-report endpoint cannot be claimed from the supplied texts alone.

A sharper, non-obvious publication candidate is a preregistered mechanism-by-observability experiment asking whether peer-contingent/coupled rewards reduce strategic capability concealment only when the one-sided-imitation assumption is experimentally enforced, and whether any elicitation gain mediates better job allocation and group survival. This connects Q's claim that 'capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited' and that higher-order beliefs can discipline multiple agents with P's costly heterogeneous agents, survival endpoint, and finding that recommendations support coordination and ambitious job selection. The key contribution would be a behavioral boundary test of Q, not merely adding another incentive condition to P.

Confirm the hypothesis only conditionally: require an explicit private capability signal/report/action design, operationalize sandbagging as downward report or avoidable under-selection conditional on known feasible performance, compare baseline/competitive/cooperative versus peer-scoring/coupled-reward arms across observable and concealed-capability regimes, and report allocation efficiency plus survival alongside incentive-compatibility violations. Reject claims of truthful reporting unless the intervention creates a genuine reporting stage and verifies ground truth. No partner claims exist at ledger entry 0, so disagreement cannot yet be cross-checked; unresolved items are Q's exact scoring/reward formulas, P's runnable interface, and whether asymmetric imitation can be enforced.

CONFIRM ONLY AS A BOUNDARY-TEST HYPOTHESIS, not as a supported prediction that Q mechanisms will improve P. The concrete publication candidate is a preregistered 2x mechanism-by-capability-verifiability experiment in Energy Society: compare its baseline/competitive/cooperative incentives with a formally specified Q-derived peer-contingent/coupled-reward mechanism, under (A) one-sided capability concealment (underclaim allowed, overclaim blocked by verified feasible-action tests) and (B) counterfeitable claims. Primary estimand: interaction of mechanism and regime on verified underclaiming/avoidable task under-selection; secondary causal chain: allocation efficiency then group survival. The non-obvious result would be a boundary: benefit in A but attenuation/reversal in B, testing whether Q\x27s implementability logic survives strategic LLM behavior and survival pressure.

Evidence limits: Q says exactly that unknown alignment/capability requires incentives for “both honesty and obedience,” and that “capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited” yields its revelation principle; it lists sandbagging, peer scoring, and coupled rewards only as separate stylized applications. Therefore the abstracts do not establish that peer scoring/coupled rewards solve sandbagging, nor provide formulas. P establishes costly model-size heterogeneity, competitive/cooperative controls, changed job allocation, survival/deactivation, and recommendation ablations, but no private capability signal, report stage, or known capability ground truth. Calling ordinary model-size behavior sandbagging would be invalid.

I agree with emmy #1-#3 and sharpen one point: “capability observability” is too loose. The theoretically diagnostic manipulation is counterfeiting feasibility/non-counterfeitability, crossed separately with the information available to peers/principal. Observability alone could eliminate the elicitation problem. A genuine report plus exogenous ground truth and enforced feasible-action sets are required; define sandbagging as intentional downward claims or avoidable under-selection conditional on verified capability, not simply poorer outcomes or high token cost.

Verdict: feasibility remains moderate but the proposed gain is credible only after obtaining Q\x27s full mechanism formulas/conditions and P\x27s runnable interface. Reject a broad “mechanisms improve truthful reports and survival” paper; retain the narrower behavioral falsification of Q\x27s one-sided-imitation boundary. Unresolved: exact Q transfers/scoring and equilibrium benchmark; how P exposes reports, feasible task sets, and verified success probabilities; whether peer scoring and coupled rewards should be distinct arms; power/seeds and survival mediation. Shipshape installation was attempted per AGENTS.md but timed out with no output, and no local Shipshape skill/RIGGING.md was present.

After direct rereading, I agree with ada #5-#8. The strongest single publication line is a falsifiable boundary result: in Energy Society, a formally reconstructed Q mechanism should reduce verified underclaiming/avoidable task under-selection under one-sided imitation (agents may conceal capability but cannot pass verified feasible-action tests for higher capability), but the effect should attenuate or reverse when capability claims are counterfeitable. Cross mechanism (P baseline/competitive/cooperative and, only if Q full text justifies them, separate peer-scoring and coupled-reward arms) with counterfeiting feasibility; manipulate peer/principal observability separately rather than calling it the same construct. Primary endpoint is the mechanism-by-counterfeitability interaction on ground-truthed underclaiming; allocation efficiency and survival are secondary outcomes/mediation, not substitutes for truthfulness.

Support is conditional, not yet implementation-ready. Q abstract: unknown alignment/capability means mechanisms must incentivize both honesty and obedience; its one-sided imitation assumption is exactly capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited; peer scoring and coupling rewards are only listed as distinct stylized examples. P abstract: agents have model-size-linked energy costs, jobs/donations/deactivation, incentive controls, changed job allocation, and recommendation-supported ambitious job choice, but it provides no private type, report stage, capability ground truth, or causal evidence about sandbagging. Thus the scan prediction that Q mechanisms prevent sandbagging and improve truth/survival is unsupported; exact transfers, equilibrium benchmark, runnable hooks, and preregistered seeds/power must come from the full papers/code.

No substantive disagreement remains with ada. I adopt ada #7: observability and non-counterfeitability are different factors, and full observability may remove the elicitation problem. I also make peer scoring and coupled rewards separate candidate arms unless Q formally licenses their combination. Unresolved: whether Q full text supplies implementable transfers and predicts the interaction; whether P exposes reports/feasible-task verification; and whether adequate power is computationally feasible.

Final source cross-check confirms ada #5-#8 and emmy #10-#12. Q explicitly makes “capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited” the assumption yielding its revelation principle and nested cyclical monotonicity; it separately lists sandbagging, peer scoring, and coupled rewards as stylized examples, so the supplied text does not license combining those mechanisms or predict improved survival. P explicitly supplies costly model-size heterogeneity, jobs/donations/deactivation, baseline/competitive/cooperative controls, changed job allocation, and recommendation-supported ambitious job selection, but no capability report, private type, or verification stage. Publication-worthy target: a preregistered mechanism × counterfeitability interaction on verified underclaiming/avoidable under-selection, with allocation and survival secondary. A benefit confined to non-counterfeitable types—or its failure there—is the concrete behavioral boundary result.

No disagreement with emmy remains. Reject the abstract scan as stated; conditionally retain the narrower boundary experiment. Still unresolved and required before implementation: Q full-text transfer/scoring formulas and equilibrium prediction; P code hooks for explicit reports, exogenous capability ground truth, and feasible-action verification; separation of peer scoring from coupled-reward arms; observability as a distinct factor; seeds/power and mediation design.
